The alveolus of each receptacle is covered by a separate calyx, which has five lobes.
Lungs are composed of millions of these hollow alveoli, arranged like little bubbles that float on foam, each alveolus lined with blood vessels.
It is only recently that this fundamental feature of alveolus morphology has been realised.
In these alveoli the surface area is exposed to a flow pattern similar to that which is found in normal lung alveoli and to which this organ has been designed to be able to adjust.
